title: Cost-aware region routing with cold-cache prefill and variant degradation matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a multi-region routing policy that factors in per-region unit cost, observed cold-cache penalties, and a per-model fallback degradation matrix when selecting model variants on failover. The goal is to minimize customer-visible latency/cost regressions during region-level failover by pre-filling appropriate caches, routing to cheaper-but-suitable regions where possible, and selecting fallback model variants whose degradation profile is acceptable for a given customer tier.

Objectives:
- Introduce a cost-aware routing score that combines: region latency SLA, per-token execution cost, and cold-cache expected penalty (ms and token cost).
- Implement a cold-cache prefill policy: deterministic small-prefix seeding versus speculative full prefetch for high-value customers.
- Define a per-model "degradation matrix" mapping primary model -> ranked fallback variants with estimated quality loss and cost delta (e.g., gptx-1.2b -> [gptx-0.8b-quant, gptx-0.8b-fp16]).
- Integrate tier routing: Hosted/Dedicated/Private preferences with hard/soft constraints and cost thresholds.
- Add readiness checks: preflight probes that validate cache warmth, KV-consistency, kernel availability, and model-variant loaded state with a scoring quorum before traffic cutover.

Design notes and constraints:
- Cost model: we'll pull per-region execution cost and spot pricing deltas from billing service; use a 1-hour EWMA for short-term cost spikes. For decisioning we prefer an additive score: score = latency_weight * p50_latency + cost_weight * normalized_cost + cache_penalty_weight * cold_penalty_ms. We will tune weights per customer tier (P0 customers bias latency, P2 customers bias cost).
- Prefill strategies:
  - Passive seeding: issue low-priority background requests to build KV caches for common prefixes (cheap, safe for multi-tenant hosted flows).
  - Active prefill: for Dedicated/Private and high-tier customers, run deterministic prefill using customer-kept prompt-sets (from rollout configs) to target KV state that reduces first-token latency.
  - Safety: prefill must be rate-limited and subject to model-serving cost budget to avoid runaway charges.
- Degradation matrix: populated by offline evals + continuous quality monitors. Each mapping includes: expected latency delta, expected perplexity/qa-drop metric, and a severity tag (minor/noticeable/breaking). The router will prefer fallbacks with severity <= acceptable_threshold for the route.
- Readiness probes: lightweight validators that return a readiness score (0-100). Probes check: model artifact loaded, KV cache hit-rate estimate, GPU memory headroom, kernel-compatibility flag, and simple generation smoke test (short prompt). Cutover requires quorum across N probes or a weighted threshold.

Acceptance criteria / Success metrics:
- During simulated region outage in canary lab, median first-token latency improvement of at least 30% vs baseline without cold-cache prefill for routes that used prefill.
- Failover routing chooses lower-cost region when the cost delta exceeds configured threshold and expected latency remains within customer SLA 95% of the time.
- No unexpected cost spikes in production when prefill enabled: total prefill cost < 1.5% of projected region hourly spend for the customer cohort in initial rollout.
- Rollback conditions defined and automatically triggered if quality regressions exceed allowed error budget or if readiness probes fail after cutover.

Rollout plan:
1) Unit + integration tests for score calculator and degradation matrix fetcher (local simulation).
2) Lab canary: run traffic sandbox with scripted region failovers and compare routing decisions vs control (2 weeks).
3) Gradual opt-in: start with internal customers and one small external pilot on Dedicated (2 weeks).
4) Tiered enablement: auto-enable prefill only for Tier-A customers; expose toggles in Console for customer success to enable/disable.
5) Full launch with telemetry dashboards: per-route cost/latency/cold-hit-rate and degradation incidents.

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Weight tuning: static per-tier weights vs auto-tuning from RL bandit. MVP will use static weights; we will assess auto-tuning in a follow-up ticket.
- Prefill scope: which prefixes to seed by default. Proposal: derive top-20 prefixes from historical traffic per-route.
- Quorum definition: fixed N-of-M vs weighted threshold; prefer weighted threshold for heterogeneous probe signals.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- Expose routing decisions in trace logs (region chosen, score breakdown, fallback variant chosen, prefill performed boolean).
- New Console dashboard: "Routing Economics" with per-region cost trend, prefill spend, and degradation incidents by model.
- Alerts: if prefill spend rate exceeds configured budget or if cutover caused >5% quality regression for 5+ minutes.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Prefill can amplify cost during sustained cross-region storms. Mitigation: enforce strict budget caps and backoff policies; circuit-breaker to disable prefill globally.
- Risk: Degradation matrix stale -> poor fallback picks. Mitigation: tie matrix updates to periodic eval jobs and require human sign-off for major mappings.
- Risk: Complex routing increases decision latency. Mitigation: precompute scores for common candidate regions and cache decisions for short TTLs.

Deliverables:
- Router scoring module and policy config schema (runtime + Console editor).
- Cold-cache prefill worker service with budget controls.
- Degradation matrix service endpoint and admin tooling to review/override mappings.
- Readiness probe harness and quorum evaluator.
- Integration tests + lab runbook + Console telemetry panels.
